meta.title: Thoreau: why most people live lives of quiet desperation

plates.query: Asher Durand Kindred Spirits Hudson River School painting
Thomas Cole lake wilderness landscape painting

beats.text: Thoreau looked at the busy, respectable people around him and saw something sad.
"The mass of men," he wrote, "lead lives of quiet desperation."
Working jobs they resent, to buy things they don't need, to impress people they don't like.
So he left. He built a cabin by a pond and lived for two years on almost nothing.
He wanted to live deliberately — to front only the essential facts of life, and not, when dying, discover he had never lived.
Simplify, he urged. Most of what we call wealth is just a heavier load to carry.
You don't need the pond. You need to ask what, in your one life, is actually essential.
